module_title: NPA Classification and Early Warning Systems (SMA)
introduction: Banks do not wake up on the 91st day surprised by an NPA. They closely monitor defaulting accounts using an early warning system called SMA. At this level, we will classify the different stages of an NPA and understand the painful concept of 'Provisioning'.

core_concepts.title: SMA (Special Mention Accounts) - The Warning Bells
core_concepts.description: Before an account hits the 90-day NPA mark, it is closely monitored: 1. SMA-0: Payment overdue between 1 to 30 days. 2. SMA-1: Overdue between 31 to 60 days. 3. SMA-2: Overdue between 61 to 90 days (Extreme High Risk).

core_concepts.title: 1. Sub-standard Asset
core_concepts.description: When a loan account crosses 90 days and officially becomes an NPA, it is first tagged as a 'Sub-standard Asset'. It remains in this category for a period of 'up to 12 months' (1 year).

core_concepts.title: 2. Doubtful Asset
core_concepts.description: If a loan account remains in the Sub-standard category for 'more than 12 months', it is downgraded to a 'Doubtful Asset'. At this stage, the bank's hopes of recovering the money drop significantly.

core_concepts.title: 3. Loss Asset
core_concepts.description: This is a loan that has been identified as a complete unrecoverable 'Loss' by the bank, internal auditors, or the RBI. Even though it might not yet be completely written off the balance sheet, its recoverable value is essentially zero.

important_entities.name: Provisioning
important_entities.significance: Under RBI rules, when a loan turns into an NPA, the bank must set aside a portion of its own 'Profits' as a safety cushion to cover the expected loss. This is called Provisioning. The older the NPA gets (moving to Doubtful or Loss), the higher the provisioning required (up to 100%), which heavily eats into the bank's net profits.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common Assertion/Reasoning trap: SMA-1 or SMA-2 accounts are NOT Non-Performing Assets. They are performing assets that are merely 'showing signs of stress'. The technical NPA tag only applies AFTER 90 days.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC and State PCS exams frequently test the exact time limit between Sub-standard and Doubtful assets. Always remember the '12 months' threshold.
